editorial_style: Single bilingual narration: Telugu connectors with English scientific, legal and programme terms; no English paragraph followed by Telugu translation
scope: Latest integrated manifest, Sections C and D only; 50 source paragraphs reviewed individually

narrative_sequence: Conflict must first be understood through the type of loss and the landscape process that caused it.
Monitoring methods must be linked to the question each method can actually answer.
Species profiles must consistently separate IUCN risk, CITES trade control and Indian legal protection.
The closing current-affairs block must distinguish an announcement, an operational programme, a survey cycle and a dated result.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Human–wildlife conflict is not simply an animal attack. It develops where the needs and movements of wildlife overlap with farms, livestock, settlements or infrastructure. The first step in mitigation is therefore to identify the actual loss—crop damage, livestock predation, injury, death or property damage—and then examine the corridor, land-use or animal-movement process behind it.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Human–wildlife conflict అంటే కేవలం ‘జంతువు దాడి’ కాదు. Wildlife movement, farms, livestock, settlements, roads వంటి human land uses ఒకదానితో ఒకటి overlap అయినప్పుడు conflict ఏర్పడుతుంది. అందువల్ల ముందుగా crop damage, livestock loss, human injury, death లేదా property damageలో ఏది జరిగిందో గుర్తించాలి. తరువాత దానికి కారణమైన corridor blockage, land-use change లేదా animal movementను పరిశీలించి mitigation measureను ఎంచుకోవాలి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The National Human–Wildlife Conflict Mitigation Strategy and Action Plan was framed for 2021–2026. It brought together early warning, rapid-response teams, suitable barriers, compensation and corridor-sensitive land-use planning. Because 2026 is the final year stated in the document, any claim that it continues unchanged after that period requires confirmation from a newer official source.
replacement_paragraphs.te: National Human–Wildlife Conflict Mitigation Strategy and Action Planను 2021–2026 period కోసం రూపొందించారు. Early-warning systems, rapid-response teams, అవసరానికి తగిన barriers, compensation, wildlife corridorsను గుర్తించే land-use planning ఇందులో భాగాలు. Documentలో పేర్కొన్న period 2026తో ముగుస్తుంది. ఆ తరువాత కూడా ఇదే plan యథాతథంగా కొనసాగుతోందని చెప్పాలంటే newer official sourceతో verify చేయాలి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Andhra Pradesh launched Project H.A.N.U.M.A.N. on 3 March 2026 as a State response to human–wildlife conflict and wildlife rescue. It combines technology-assisted monitoring with field response: AI-based alerts and GPS tracking can indicate risky elephant movement, while dedicated teams, rescue vehicles and treatment facilities support action on the ground.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Andhra Pradesh 3 March 2026న Project H.A.N.U.M.A.N.ను human–wildlife conflict response, wildlife rescue కోసం ప్రారంభించింది. ఇందులో technology, field response రెండూ కలిసి పనిచేస్తాయి. AI-based alerts, elephant GPS tracking ద్వారా risky movementను ముందుగా గుర్తించవచ్చు; dedicated teams, rescue vehicles, treatment facilities ద్వారా ground-level action తీసుకుంటారు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Different conflicts require different remedies. Crop-raiding by elephants or wild boar may call for barriers, deterrents and crop protection; livestock predation by leopards, snow leopards or wolves may require predator-resistant enclosures. Where direct encounters can injure or kill people, reliable early warning and trained rapid response become essential. A single generic remedy cannot address every form of conflict.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Conflict రకాన్ని బట్టి remedy మారుతుంది. Elephants లేదా wild boar వల్ల crop damage జరిగితే barriers, deterrents, crop protection ఉపయోగపడవచ్చు. Leopards, snow leopards లేదా wolves livestockను చంపే ప్రాంతాల్లో predator-resistant enclosures అవసరం. Direct encounter వల్ల human injury లేదా death risk ఉన్నప్పుడు reliable early warning, trained rapid response అత్యవసరం. కాబట్టి అన్ని conflictsకు ఒకే generic solution సరిపోదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: A monitoring method should be chosen for the question being asked. Camera-trap mark–recapture estimates abundance when individuals can be recognised from markings. Genetic samples from dung, hair or other material can identify individuals; telemetry follows movement; transects and sign surveys estimate occurrence or density; and environmental DNA detects genetic traces left in water or soil. A population number is interpretable only with its method, area and survey year.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Monitoring methodను research questionకు సరిపడేలా ఎంచుకోవాలి. Individual markings స్పష్టంగా ఉన్న speciesలో camera-trap mark–recapture ద్వారా abundanceను estimate చేయవచ్చు. Dung, hair వంటి samplesలో genetic analysis individualsను గుర్తిస్తుంది; telemetry movementను track చేస్తుంది; transects, sign surveys presence లేదా densityను అంచనా వేస్తాయి; environmental DNA నీరు లేదా నేలలో మిగిలిన genetic tracesను గుర్తిస్తుంది. Method, study area, survey year లేకుండా population figureకు పూర్తి అర్థం ఉండదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India introduced M-STrIPES in 2010 for digital management and monitoring in tiger reserves. It integrates field observations with GPS/GPRS, remote sensing and GIS to record patrol effort, ecological observations and conflict information. It strengthens protection and spatial monitoring, but it is not by itself an independent wildlife-population estimation method.
replacement_paragraphs.te: NTCA, Wildlife Institute of India కలిసి 2010లో M-STrIPESను tiger reservesలో digital management, monitoring కోసం ప్రవేశపెట్టాయి. Field observationsను GPS/GPRS, remote sensing, GISతో కలిపి patrol effort, ecological observations, conflict informationను record చేస్తుంది. ఇది protection, spatial monitoringను బలపరుస్తుంది; కానీ స్వతంత్ర wildlife-population estimation method కాదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The tiger and Asian elephant are both Endangered globally and listed in CITES Appendix I, while Indian law gives them its highest level of animal protection. Project Tiger and NTCA focus on tiger landscapes; Project Elephant covers Asian elephants, their habitats, corridors, conflict mitigation and captive-elephant welfare. The Asian elephant must not be confused with the African savanna elephant or the Critically Endangered African forest elephant. India's 2021–25 genetic assessment estimated about 22,446 wild Asian elephants, but it created a new methodological baseline rather than a directly comparable continuation of earlier visual counts.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Tiger, Asian elephant రెండూ IUCNలో Endangered (EN), CITES Appendix Iలో ఉన్నాయి; Indian wildlife law కింద highest animal protection పొందుతాయి. Project Tiger, NTCA tiger landscapesపై focus చేస్తే, Project Elephant Asian elephants, habitats, corridors, conflict mitigation, captive-elephant welfareను cover చేస్తుంది. Asian elephantను African savanna elephantతో లేదా Critically Endangered African forest elephantతో కలపకూడదు. India's 2021–25 genetic assessment సుమారు 22,446 wild Asian elephantsను estimate చేసింది; method మారినందున ఇది earlier visual countsకు direct continuation కాదు, new baseline.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The 2021–25 elephant assessment estimated 22,446 animals, within a range of 18,255–26,645. Two 2017 totals—27,312 and 29,964—produce different headline declines when used as comparators. More importantly, the new exercise used dung-DNA genetic mark–recapture, whereas the earlier exercise relied on direct counts and physical identification. The apparent percentages therefore must not be presented as clean population trends.
replacement_paragraphs.te: 2021–25 elephant assessmentలో estimate 22,446; probable range 18,255–26,645. 2017కు 27,312, 29,964 అనే రెండు totals వాడుకలో ఉండటంతో comparatorను బట్టి headline decline మారుతుంది. ముఖ్యంగా new assessment dung-DNA genetic mark–recaptureను ఉపయోగించగా, earlier exercise direct counts, physical identificationపై ఆధారపడింది. అందువల్ల కనిపించే percentage differenceను clean population trendగా చెప్పకూడదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Jerdon's Courser is a Critically Endangered nocturnal bird of scrub forest and is strictly protected in India; it is not listed in a CITES Appendix. Rediscovered in Andhra Pradesh in 1986 after decades without a record, it was last confirmed around 2004. BirdLife International and Mongabay India reported an acoustic detection in the wider Lankamalla Hills on 24 August 2025, outside Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary. Because that evidence had not yet been published in a peer-reviewed paper, it should be presented as a provisional, attributed report rather than a confirmed rediscovery.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Jerdon's Courser ఒక Critically Endangered nocturnal scrub-forest bird. Indiaలో strict legal protection పొందుతుంది; ఇది ఏ CITES Appendixలోనూ listed కాదు. దశాబ్దాలపాటు record లేకపోయిన తరువాత 1986లో Andhra Pradeshలో rediscover చేశారు; last confirmed record సుమారు 2004. 24 August 2025న Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary వెలుపల wider Lankamalla Hillsలో acoustic detection జరిగినట్లు BirdLife International, Mongabay India report చేశాయి. Peer-reviewed publication ఇంకా లేనందున దీన్ని confirmed rediscoveryగా కాకుండా attributed provisional reportగా మాత్రమే రాయాలి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Red sanders is endemic to the southern Eastern Ghats, especially the Seshachalam–Chittoor region of Andhra Pradesh, and is a specially protected plant under Indian law. Its CITES Appendix II listing regulates international trade; it does not mean that every lawful transaction is prohibited. Red sanders and fragrant sandalwood are different species in different genera. Overseas demand for furniture and musical instruments drives much of the smuggling, which Andhra Pradesh combats through a specialised task force.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Red sanders southern Eastern Ghatsకు endemic; ముఖ్యంగా Andhra Pradeshలోని Seshachalam–Chittoor regionతో ముడిపడి ఉంది. Indian lawలో specially protected plant. CITES Appendix II listing international tradeను regulate చేస్తుంది; ప్రతి lawful transactionను పూర్తిగా prohibit చేయదు. Red sanders, fragrant sandalwood వేర్వేరు generaకు చెందిన వేర్వేరు trees. Furniture, musical instruments కోసం overseas demand smugglingను పెంచుతుంది; Andhra Pradesh specialised task force దీనిపై action తీసుకుంటుంది.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The Nilgiri tahr is an Endangered Western Ghats endemic and Tamil Nadu's State Animal. It occupies the montane shola–grassland mosaic, broadly around 1,200–2,600 metres, and its largest population occurs in Eravikulam National Park. Tamil Nadu launched Project Nilgiri Tahr in 2023, and Tamil Nadu and Kerala conducted their first synchronised estimate in April 2025. Reports gave totals near 2,668 or 2,655 because the cited Kerala count differed slightly. It is distinct from the Himalayan tahr and is not listed in a CITES Appendix.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Nilgiri tahr ఒక Endangered Western Ghats endemic species; Tamil Nadu State Animal కూడా. సాధారణంగా 1,200–2,600 metres ఎత్తులోని montane shola–grassland mosaicలో జీవిస్తుంది; largest population Eravikulam National Parkలో ఉంది. Tamil Nadu 2023లో Project Nilgiri Tahrను ప్రారంభించింది. Tamil Nadu, Kerala April 2025లో first synchronised estimate నిర్వహించాయి. Kerala countలో source difference వల్ల total కొన్ని reportsలో 2,668, మరికొన్నింటిలో 2,655గా వచ్చింది. ఇది Himalayan tahrకు భిన్నమైన species; ఏ CITES Appendixలోనూ లేదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The National Wildlife Action Plan 2017–2031 is India's third comprehensive wildlife action plan. It is organised into five components, 17 themes, 103 actions and 250 projects, and notably mainstreams climate-change concerns across wildlife policy. It is an overarching framework, not a substitute for species-specific mechanisms such as Project Tiger or Project Elephant.
replacement_paragraphs.te: National Wildlife Action Plan 2017–2031, India's third comprehensive wildlife action plan. ఇందులో 5 components, 17 themes, 103 actions, 250 projects ఉన్నాయి. Wildlife policy అంతటా climate-change concernsను mainstream చేయడం దీని ముఖ్య లక్షణం. ఇది overarching framework మాత్రమే; Project Tiger, Project Elephant వంటి species-specific mechanismsకు replacement కాదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Four initiatives—Project Sloth Bear, Project Gharial, Tigers Outside Tiger Reserves and Project Dolphin Phase II—were unveiled together on 6 October 2025 during Wildlife Week. The Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict belongs to a different event: it was announced on 3 March 2025 and inaugurated on 10 July 2026. Andhra Pradesh's Project H.A.N.U.M.A.N., launched on 3 March 2026, is a third and separate initiative. Similar subject matter must not be used to merge these three policy events.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Project Sloth Bear, Project Gharial, Tigers Outside Tiger Reserves, Project Dolphin Phase II అనే four initiativesను Wildlife Weekలో 6 October 2025న కలిసి unveil చేశారు. Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict వేరే event: 3 March 2025న announce చేసి, 10 July 2026న inaugurate చేశారు. Andhra Pradesh Project H.A.N.U.M.A.N.ను 3 March 2026న launch చేసింది. Subject similarగా ఉన్నా, ఈ three policy eventsను ఒకే packageగా కలపకూడదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Gujarat's sixteenth Asiatic lion estimation recorded 891 lions in 2025. Cheetah totals are far more date-sensitive because births, deaths and translocations can change them within days: official reporting gave 57 on 10 May 2026 and about 53 on 13 May after four cub deaths, with 50 at Kuno and three at Gandhi Sagar. Lion and cheetah figures must therefore be attached to their census or reporting date.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Gujaratలో 2025లో జరిగిన 16th Asiatic lion estimation 891 lionsను record చేసింది. Cheetah total births, deaths, translocations వల్ల కొద్ది రోజుల్లోనే మారవచ్చు. Official reporting ప్రకారం 10 May 2026న 57 ఉండగా, four cub deaths తరువాత 13 Mayన సుమారు 53—Kunoలో 50, Gandhi Sagarలో 3—మిగిలాయి. కాబట్టి lion, cheetah figuresను census లేదా reporting date లేకుండా quote చేయకూడదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: India's first comprehensive river-dolphin census, released in 2025, estimated about 6,327 dolphins. A second range-wide assessment began under Project Dolphin Phase II in January 2026. The Snow Leopard Population Assessment in India used 2019–2023 fieldwork and reported an estimate of 718 in 2024, establishing a first national baseline. Neither figure should be detached from its survey period and method.
replacement_paragraphs.te: India's first comprehensive river-dolphin censusను 2025లో release చేసి సుమారు 6,327 dolphinsను estimate చేశారు. Comparable follow-up కోసం Project Dolphin Phase II కింద January 2026లో second range-wide assessment ప్రారంభమైంది. Snow Leopard Population Assessment in India, 2019–2023 fieldwork ఆధారంగా 2024లో 718 అనే estimate ఇచ్చి first national baselineను ఏర్పరచింది. ఈ రెండు figuresనూ survey period, method నుంచి విడదీసి చదవకూడదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: At the stated reference dates, India had 18 nationally designated Biosphere Reserves, 13 of them in UNESCO's World Network, and 101 Ramsar Sites in August 2026. These are different recognition systems: domestic Biosphere Reserve designation does not automatically confer UNESCO status, while Ramsar designation identifies wetlands of international importance. Both totals are date-sensitive.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Stated reference dates ప్రకారం Indiaలో nationally designated Biosphere Reserves 18; వాటిలో UNESCO World Networkలో 13 ఉన్నాయి. August 2026 నాటికి Ramsar Sites 101. ఇవి separate recognition systems. Domestic Biosphere Reserve designationతో automaticగా UNESCO status రాదు; Ramsar designation wetlands of international importanceకు వర్తిస్తుంది. New formal recognitionsతో రెండు totals మారవచ్చు కాబట్టి date తప్పనిసరి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: A programme name does not by itself prove statutory authority or continuing operation. For every initiative, identify the responsible institution, its legal or executive basis, launch date, stated period and measurable function. Any changing total or operational claim must carry a reference date.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Programmeకు official-sounding name ఉందనే కారణంతో అది statutory authority అవదు; ఇప్పటికీ operate అవుతోందని కూడా నిర్ధారణ కాదు. ప్రతి initiativeలో responsible institution, legal లేదా executive basis, launch date, stated period, measurable functionను గుర్తించాలి. మారే total లేదా operational claimను reference dateతోనే రాయాలి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: MISHTI—Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes—was announced in the 2023–24 Union Budget on 1 February 2023 and launched on 5 June 2023. From financial year 2023–24 it set a five-year target of restoring or planting mangroves over about 540 sq km. Its 80:20 Union–State pattern works mainly through convergence with mechanisms such as MGNREGS and CAMPA. It joins coastal protection and blue-carbon storage with livelihood benefits across 13 coastal States and Union Territories; differing 11+2 or 9+4 break-ups should be attributed to their source.
replacement_paragraphs.te: MISHTI పూర్తి రూపం Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes. 2023–24 Union Budgetలో 1 February 2023న announce చేసి, 5 June 2023న launch చేశారు. FY 2023–24 నుంచి five yearsలో సుమారు 540 sq km mangrovesను restore లేదా plant చేయడం target. Union–State funding pattern 80:20; implementation ప్రధానంగా MGNREGS, CAMPA వంటి mechanismsతో convergence ద్వారా సాగుతుంది. Coastal protection, blue-carbon storage, livelihoodsను 13 coastal States and Union Territoriesలో కలుపుతుంది. 11+2 లేదా 9+4 breakupను వాడితే sourceను తప్పనిసరిగా చెప్పాలి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Amrit Dharohar is a three-year MoEFCC scheme for capacity building and community participation at sites that already possess Ramsar designation. Announced alongside MISHTI and launched on 5 June 2023, it applies the Ramsar principle of wise use through biodiversity conservation, carbon-stock assessment, eco-tourism, green jobs and community stewardship. It neither designates new Ramsar Sites nor replaces the Ramsar Convention.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Amrit Dharohar, Ramsar designation ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న sitesలో capacity building, community participation కోసం MoEFCC చేపట్టిన three-year scheme. MISHTIతో పాటు announce చేసి 5 June 2023న launch చేశారు. Biodiversity conservation, carbon-stock assessment, eco-tourism, green jobs, community stewardship ద్వారా Ramsar ‘wise use’ principleను అమలు చేస్తుంది. ఇది new Ramsar Sitesను designate చేయదు; Ramsar Conventionకు replacement కూడా కాదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: IUCN categories assess global extinction risk, CITES Appendices regulate international trade and Wildlife Protection Act Schedules provide legal protection within India. Wildlife-crime institutions also have distinct functions: WCCB coordinates intelligence and links with CITES enforcement, while DRI acts against customs and smuggling offences. The CITES Management Authority and Scientific Authority likewise perform separate regulatory and scientific roles.
replacement_paragraphs.te: IUCN category global extinction riskను assess చేస్తుంది; CITES Appendix international tradeను regulate చేస్తుంది; Wildlife Protection Act Schedule Indiaలో legal protectionను ఇస్తుంది. Enforcement institutions roles కూడా వేరు. WCCB wildlife-crime intelligenceను coordinate చేసి CITES enforcementతో link అవుతుంది; DRI customs, smuggling offencesపై action తీసుకుంటుంది. CITES Management Authority, Scientific Authority కూడా separate regulatory, scientific functions నిర్వహిస్తాయి.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The Indian star tortoise was transferred to CITES Appendix I at CoP18 in 2019 in response to commercial pet trade. Red sanders has remained in Appendix II since 1994, so legal international trade is regulated rather than absolutely prohibited; illegal logging remains a separate offence. All pangolin species moved to Appendix I at CoP17 in 2016. Review of Significant Trade decisions and seizure figures are dated enforcement evidence, not permanent conservation-status labels.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Commercial pet tradeను curb చేయడానికి Indian star tortoiseను CITES CoP18లో 2019లో Appendix Iకు transfer చేశారు. Red sanders 1994 నుంచి Appendix IIలో ఉంది; legal international trade regulated, absolute prohibition కాదు. Illegal logging మాత్రం separate offence. అన్ని pangolin speciesను CoP17లో 2016లో Appendix Iకు మార్చారు. Review of Significant Trade decisions, seizure figures dated enforcement evidence మాత్రమే; permanent conservation-status labels కావు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: The International Big Cat Alliance is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation for cooperation, knowledge sharing, capacity building, anti-trafficking practice and resource mobilisation. It is neither an Indian field-level species project nor a statutory authority under the Wildlife Protection Act. Announced on 9 April 2023, it received Union Cabinet approval on 29 February 2024 for establishment and an Indian headquarters, with ₹150 crore over five years. Its Framework Agreement entered into force on 23 January 2025 after five founding ratifications, and the Headquarters Agreement followed on 17 April 2025.
replacement_paragraphs.te: International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) cooperation, knowledge sharing, capacity building, anti-trafficking practice, resource mobilisation కోసం treaty-based intergovernmental organisation. ఇది Indian field-level species project కాదు; Wildlife Protection Act కింద statutory authority కూడా కాదు. 9 April 2023న announce చేశారు. Indiaలో headquarters, five yearsకు ₹150 crore supportతో establishmentను Union Cabinet 29 February 2024న approve చేసింది. Five founding ratifications తరువాత Framework Agreement 23 January 2025న forceలోకి వచ్చింది; Headquarters Agreement 17 April 2025న జరిగింది.

replacement_paragraphs.en: IBCA covers tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. Clouded leopard and lynx are not included. The first five occur in India, whereas jaguar and puma are native to the Americas. The figure 95 or 96 refers to potential range countries, not current members. Its first summit, planned for 1–2 June 2026, was postponed by a PIB notice dated 21 May 2026, so the planned meeting did not produce a New Delhi Declaration.
replacement_paragraphs.te: IBCA cover చేసే seven species: tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma. Clouded leopard, lynx ఈ listలో లేవు. First five Indiaలో occur అవుతాయి; jaguar, puma Americasకు native. 95 లేదా 96 అనేది potential range countries figure; current members count కాదు. 1–2 June 2026కు planned first summitను 21 May 2026 PIB notice ద్వారా postpone చేశారు. కాబట్టి planned meeting నుంచి New Delhi Declaration వచ్చిందని చెప్పడం తప్పు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Operation Olivia is an annual Indian Coast Guard operation under the Ministry of Defence, not an MoEFCC project. Conducted since the early 1980s, generally from November to May off Odisha's nesting coast, it uses surface and aerial patrols, seasonal trawling restrictions and enforcement of Turtle Excluder Devices to reduce olive-ridley deaths in trawl nets. Patrol effort and turtle counts vary by season and require dates.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Operation Olivia, Ministry of Defence కింద Indian Coast Guard annually నిర్వహించే operation; MoEFCC project కాదు. Early 1980s నుంచి Odisha nesting coast watersలో సాధారణంగా November–May మధ్య నిర్వహిస్తున్నారు. Surface patrols, aerial patrols, seasonal trawling restrictions, Turtle Excluder Devices enforcement ద్వారా olive ridleys trawl netsలో చిక్కి మునిగే ప్రమాదాన్ని తగ్గిస్తుంది. Patrol effort, turtle counts seasonను బట్టి మారుతాయి కాబట్టి date అవసరం.

replacement_paragraphs.en: MoEFCC released the National Marine Turtle Action Plan 2021–2026 on 28 January 2021 together with the Marine Mega Fauna Stranding Guidelines. It coordinates threat reduction, habitat rehabilitation, response to stranding and entanglement, research and community participation across agencies. Since its stated cycle ends in 2026, a successor or extension must be verified before it is described as the current plan.
replacement_paragraphs.te: MoEFCC, National Marine Turtle Action Plan 2021–2026ను Marine Mega Fauna Stranding Guidelinesతో కలిసి 28 January 2021న release చేసింది. Threat reduction, habitat rehabilitation, stranding లేదా entanglement response, research, community participationను agencies మధ్య coordinate చేస్తుంది. Stated cycle 2026తో ముగుస్తుంది; successor లేదా extensionను verify చేయకుండా దీన్ని current planగా పేర్కొనకూడదు.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Project Hangul is a Jammu and Kashmir State initiative begun in the 1970s with IUCN and WWF support for the Critically Endangered Kashmir stag, now concentrated mainly in Dachigam National Park. Sangai is a different species: Manipur's Endangered brow-antlered deer, living on floating phumdi in Keibul Lamjao National Park on Loktak Lake. The two differ in species, State, habitat and programme history, though both demonstrate the risk of concentration at one principal site.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Project Hangul, 1970sలో IUCN, WWF supportతో ప్రారంభమైన Jammu and Kashmir State initiative. Critically Endangered Kashmir stag ఇప్పుడు mainly Dachigam National Parkలో concentratedగా ఉంది. Sangai వేరే species: Manipurకు చెందిన Endangered brow-antlered deer; Loktak Lakeలో floating phumdiపై ఉన్న Keibul Lamjao National Parkలో జీవిస్తుంది. Species, State, habitat, programme history అన్నీ వేరు; అయితే single principal siteలో population concentrate అవడం వల్ల వచ్చే risk రెండింటికీ common.

replacement_paragraphs.en: Indian Rhino Vision 2020 was a multi-partner vision launched in 2005, not a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Returning wild rhinos to Manas, where they had disappeared locally, was reintroduction rather than reinforcement. India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was notified on 21 September 2022 over 448.34 sq km of seagrass habitat in northern Palk Bay; it is a Conservation Reserve, not a National Park. Project Nilgiri Tahr is a Tamil Nadu State project launched in 2023, and Tamil Nadu and Kerala conducted a synchronised estimate in April 2025.
replacement_paragraphs.te: Indian Rhino Vision 2020, 2005లో launch చేసిన multi-partner vision; Centrally Sponsored Scheme కాదు. Rhinos locally disappear అయిన Manasకు wild animalsను తిరిగి release చేయడం reintroduction, reinforcement కాదు. India's first Dugong Conservation Reserveను northern Palk Bayలోని 448.34 sq km seagrass habitatపై 21 September 2022న notify చేశారు; legal category Conservation Reserve, National Park కాదు. Project Nilgiri Tahr 2023లో launch అయిన Tamil Nadu State project; Tamil Nadu, Kerala April 2025లో synchronised estimate నిర్వహించాయి.

accuracy_and_coverage_flags: Section C's mapped MCQ list contains four duplicated integrations: st3-int-b-q002, st3-int-b-q012, st3-int-b-q013 and st3-int-b-q014 each appears twice.

The source metadata is too narrow for several 2025–2026 claims. canonical-html, CITES, IUCN and NTCA do not independently support AP Project H.A.N.U.M.A.N., the July 2026 HWC centre inauguration, 2026 cheetah totals, August 2026 Ramsar total or the postponed IBCA summit.
Current date is 12 October 2026. Every post-2025 operational statistic must retain its date and should be rechecked against the originating government release before final publication.

The elephant figure 22,446 must be described as a new genetic-method baseline. Percent decline questions against 2017 are pedagogically unsafe unless the comparator and method discontinuity are stated.
The two tiger figures, 3,682 and 3,652, cannot appear as interchangeable correct answers; each must retain its official source label.
Jerdon's Courser acoustic evidence reported for 24 August 2025 is provisional unless a peer-reviewed or official confirmation has since appeared.
Nilgiri tahr has strict Indian protection but no CITES Appendix listing; questions must test this distinction rather than silently equate WPA protection with CITES status.
The planned IBCA summit was postponed; no MCQ should presuppose that the planned June 2026 meeting produced a New Delhi Declaration.
Plan periods ending in 2025 or 2026 should be described historically unless an official successor or extension is documented.

Add a chronology question distinguishing the four-project Wildlife Week package, the HWC Centre and Andhra Pradesh's Project H.A.N.U.M.A.N.
